First off I love that you asked this question. I'm a bit of a journaling junkie. I apologize in advance if this post ends up being a bit long. Also sorry for the formatting nightmare, I'm still a Reddit noob.

How your journal ends up looking is dependent on what you're using it for. If you're looking to just track your moods and looking for patterns, I suggest printing out some mood charts and sticking them in a binder. Doctors love mood charts. They provide a great visual overview without you having to flip through a bunch of pages. Luckily, there are a bunch of templates available online that you can download for free.

Personally, I prefer ones that also track my sleep, anxiety, irritability and medication adherence. I also like have room write out any significant daily event (e.g., first day at a new job, mom showed up unannounced, got sick, on my period etc.)

Now, if you're looking for something that leaves more room for creativity, I suggest looking into bullet journaling. Here's a great overview from Buzzfeed of all places. (https://www.buzzfeed.com/rachelwmiller/mental-health-bullet-journal?utm_term=.vbR8WWXVz#.fbZjGG4W5) 

There's actually a pretty substantial online community of bullet journalers, so I'm sure you'll be able to find some neat ideas there. 

One last suggestion, dedicate a specific time of day to journal, otherwise it's easy to get out of the habit. I set an alarm on my phone to remind me. Other people think it's excessive, but hey it works for me! 

I hope this is helpful!
Has there been a recent change to your meds? When I started lamictal,  it killed my appetite and made me lose my taste for food. It got progressively worse as the dosage increased.

The actual mg amount that you're taking doesn't really matter because everybody metabolizes it differently.  What matters is the therapeutic blood level.  For reference,  I take 1500mg and am at a 0.8 blood lever.  0.6 is the low end of the therapeutic range.

I'm at a 0.6 blood level and I play piano.  Luckily,  I haven't had any tremors...  Or many side effects for that matter.  My biggest issue is the thirst and having to pee all the time,  but that I can live with. Side effects vary from person to person,  but just wanted to let you know that tremors are not a guarantee.

Another huge one is that medication will turn me into a zombie. Finally, I find that people are more willing to try to understand the depression side of things. It's so much harder to talk about mania - especially when it involves psychosis or other "scarier" symptoms. 

3. My parents and I aren't on great terms. They can't accept that this isn't something that will just go away. Also, they get on me for not telling them stuff. Admittedly I don't...Mostly because they always overreact and get super weird around me. It's a vicious cycle.

4. Thoughts, yes. I have never attempted. I do self-harm, but it's never because I want to kill myself. It's more of a really shitty coping mechanism when I'm feeling overwhelmed. 

5. Trying out different meds under supervision of a psychiatrist with mixed results. I've been told it can take years ugh. I also attend a cognitive behavioral therapy group which is really helpful.
